title: Connect findings from two studies
objective: Write a conclusion that uses evidence from both studies.

slides.title: Build a comparison
body: Find the question, measure and setting in each study.
Look for a shared pattern or a difference. Explain which details support that judgement.

slides.title: Read two class examples
body: Lettuce mean dry mass rose from 7.9 g to 12.6 g as daily light rose from 4 to 8 hours.
Spinach mean leaf count rose from 7 to 11 as daily light rose from 6 to 10 hours.
Model: Both measures rose with longer light periods. Grams and leaf counts describe different things.

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Report A: A team saw more frogs at a shaded pond than at an open pond on one morning. Report B: Another team saw similar numbers at two ponds on one evening.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: State the main finding of each report.
Compare the reports in one sentence. Use “while” or “however”.
Write one short line per report.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Report A: A team saw more bees in a sunny garden than in a shaded garden on one morning. Report B: Another team saw similar numbers in two gardens on one evening.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: State the main finding of each report.
Compare the reports in one sentence. Use “while” or “however”.
Suggest one reason the findings may differ and one way to check it.

slides.title: Check the link
body: Point to the idea from each study in your conclusion. Which word shows how the ideas connect?
